Now the Sultan kept his forces away from the city,
and laid them in ambush in the mountains;
and everyone who went out they would capture.
And when they had remained for some time thus in distress,
they sent to the Sultan,
and surrendered the city to him.
And the Turks and Greeks joined together in fighting against the Franks.
And the Sultan took its citadel,
and took the Franks who were in it as captives;
and he also took Chonas {Konas}.
And in this year, when Muhammad son of Bukhtamar had grown up,
the ruler of Khilat,
he killed Hezardinar, his brother-in-law,
the one who had killed his father.
And because he was young, he began to live dissolutely,
and the people of Khilat hated him.
Also an emir, one of the slaves of the Shah-Arman,
whose name was Balaban,
rebelled against him in Manazgird.
Then certain men of the people of Khilat sent to Nasir al-Din Artuq, son of Ilghazi, son of Alpi, son of Timurtash, son of Ilghazi, son of Artuq, the lord of Mardin, and said to him:
"This cousin of your father is not capable of surviving;
come therefore, and we will surrender Khilat to you."
And when the lord of Mardin went,
and with him forces of Turks and of the Ma'addites {Arabs},
they repented (they were divided) {OCR?}:
because they saw that those who were with him were famished,
and they feared lest they should plunder them;
and they prepared for war.
Then Balaban sent to the lord of Mardin and said to him:
"The people of Khilat shrink from the Ma'addites who are with you.
Therefore move away from Khilat,
and I will manage your affair."
And when he turned back {OCR?}, Balaban sent threats to the lord of Mardin,
if he did not go back to his own country.
And because those who were with him were few,
he was afraid, and left and went away;
he found his country plundered by al-Malik al-Ashraf.
For that al-Ashraf had dwelt in Dunaysir,
and had collected much property from it, and left and went to Harran.
Then Balaban gathered an army and came against Khilat,
and was not able to take it by war.
However, when he multiplied promises of good things to the people of Khilat,
and swore strong oaths to them
that he would not harm even the smallest of them,
they surrendered to him.
And when he entered,
he imprisoned the son of Bukhtamar in one of the fortresses;
and then he became more strengthened.
